parsed.explanation: Strong positives: no criminalisation, legal gender recognition (1986, no-surgery 2015, dead-name removal 2024), enhanced hate-crime penalties, courts ruling for trans people (2019 prison transfer/HRT, 2020 service refusal, 2025 certificate), and documented mass social acceptance (250,000-strong Pride, majority marriage support). But traveller-facing exposures pull it down: the main airport has no trans-screening regulation and a documented 2023 humiliating gender-identity screening outing a traveller; custody defaults to isolation/segregation with trans women held in men's prisons, no placement statute, and visitor relief unestablished (tier-1 state exposure); and 2025 saw a record 433 physical homophobic/transphobic incidents including organised ambushes with trans people bearing the brunt — a documented pattern, though raw counts lack denominators and the state's response (hate-crime enhancement, functioning courts) is protective. Lethal pride attacks are dated (2005–2015). Net: elevated risk from unremedied state exposures plus rising hostility despite good law.
